insider_note: The third transfer, and the one that uses a virus. Lederberg and Zinder, in Salmonella typhimurium.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What transduction is
steps.margin_note: Definition naming the bacteriophage. Three lines.
lines: TRANSDUCTION is the transfer of genetic material
from one bacterium to another THROUGH A
BACTERIOPHAGE, that is, through a virus.
steps.why: The virus does the carrying, so no contact between the two bacteria is needed at any point.
common_mistakes: Writing 'bacterio phase'. The carrier is a BACTERIOPHAGE, a virus.
Saying the two cells touch. In transduction they never need to meet.

steps.label: Who and where
steps.margin_note: Both names, the organism, and the three-way list as a check.
lines: It was discovered by LEDERBERG and ZINDER.
The three transfers together are conjugation,
steps.why: Listing all three at the end is the fastest check that the right names have gone with the right process, because Lederberg appears in two of them.
common_mistakes: Naming Tatum. Tatum worked with Lederberg on CONJUGATION, not transduction.
Naming E. coli. Transduction was shown in Salmonella typhimurium.
steps.memory_tip: Zinder goes with Salmonella; Tatum goes with E. coli.
